purpose: Wording that makes prose read as machine-generated. scripts/check-copy.mjs fails CI on block entries in visible site copy and reports warn entries.
method: Five independent source sweeps (quantitative excess-vocabulary studies, open-source slop lists, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, editorial and practitioner guides for web copy, curated local style registries), merged and deduplicated, then adversarially verified: sources reopened, regexes compiled and probed against technical prose, false-positive risks for an Apple Neural Engine measurement site downgraded or narrowed. Every entry cites at least one source that was opened.

categories.description: Words measured as over-represented in LLM-era academic prose.
Praise or significance language that asserts importance without evidence.
Marketing or promotional verbs that replace a measured change.
Adjectives that assert quality or novelty without a test or number.
Stock marketing phrases and claims.
Connectors and openers that add words without content.
Hedges and signposts that announce uncertainty or considerations instead of stating them.
Recap labels that close text with a restatement.
Scene-setting phrases that sound broad but name nothing.
Replacing plain 'is' with fancier verbs such as serves as or stands as.
Formulas that inflate a result into symbolic importance.
Tacked-on interpretation clauses and vague praise for insights.
Denying a claim nobody made, then supplying a replacement.
Em dash and dash-substitute punctuation, measured as density.
Assistant self-reference, acknowledgements and sign-offs pasted into copy.
Unnamed authorities used to borrow weight.
Template that lists challenges and ends on vague positivity.
Template section titles typical of generated outlines.
Markdown formatting that leaks into rendered prose.
Unfilled template placeholders, dates and URLs.
Assistant-origin tracking parameters on links.
Emoji used as icons, bullets or heading markers.
Unsourced precision, rankings or magnitudes.
Round user counts and social proof with no named source.
Slogans the owner rejected; sourced to the owner statement, not to a fetched URL.
Link and button labels that name no destination.
Editorial or intimacy labels that decorate a section.
Decorative page chrome that adds no content.

integrator: field-notes-label widened to the singular after a manual read found "field note" labels the plural pattern missed
dropped_during_merge: NOTE: Source lists are trimmed to 1-5 URLs per entry for output size; source_count matches the listed URLs, not the full raw union. I did not re-open the sources in this merge step; sourcing is as reported by the five sweeps. Entries whose only source is the owner statement are kept and labelled owner:2026-11-08 rather than a fetched URL.
Dropped 'findings' (warn-level, common in research prose, no per-word evidence) and 'potential' (too generic; legitimate everywhere).
Dropped 'significant' (legitimate statistical term; Geng & Trotta measured no magnitude).
Dropped 'finally,' (vendor count with no rate; legitimate sequencing word).
Dropped 'in connection with' and 'in association with' (ordinary English, low precision).
Dropped 'a X rather than a Y' (too broad; correct technical contrast is common).
Dropped the ALL-CAPS passage rule: the checker adds the i flag, so the case-sensitive test cannot be enforced.
Dropped bare 'in today's' and 'overall,' closers (folded into the in-today's opener or too generic).
Dropped separate 'should not be confused with' variant as low precision; contributing-to kept at warn.
Merged duplicate entries from the raw sweeps (delve variants, crucial, meticulous, showcase, em dash, emoji, and similar), so the same meaning appears once.
Kind values normalised to the schema enum (word, phrase, structure, punctuation); the raw category slugs were moved into category.

entries.why: Most-measured excess word in LLM-era academic prose, so it reads as model vocabulary.
entries.evidence: Kobak et al.: 'delves' excess ratio r=28.0 in 2024 PubMed abstracts; Juzek & Ward name it as a focal word.
entries.example: Let's delve into how the ANE schedules each layer.
entries.replacement_hint: Say 'look at' or name the thing examined.

entries.why: Stock significance formula that asserts importance instead of showing it.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia lists 'underscores its importance/significance' as a watch phrase.
entries.example: These results underscore the importance of batch size.
entries.replacement_hint: Show the batch-size curve.

entries.why: Measured excess verb in 2024 abstracts and a listed AI-vocabulary item.
entries.evidence: Kobak et al.: 'underscores' r=13.8; Language Log cites a nine-fold rise.
entries.example: These results underscore the cache effect.
entries.replacement_hint: Use 'show' or 'mean'.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Identifier or character named underscore; skip code spans.

entries.why: Promotional verb that replaces plain 'shows' in LLM text.
entries.evidence: Kobak et al.: 'showcasing' r=10.7; Liang et al. list it among the four most LLM-skewed words.
entries.example: The benchmark showcases a 2x speedup on the Neural Engine.
entries.replacement_hint: Use 'shows' and give the figure.

entries.why: Grandiose noun for ordinary domains; top LLM-preferred word in one measurement.
entries.evidence: Liang et al. Fig 2 caption: among four words most skewed toward LLMs (log odds).
entries.example: This sits in the realm of low-latency inference.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the area: 'This is a low-latency inference question.'
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Occasionally literal in physics or CS prose.

entries.why: Stock complexity intensifier that LLMs favour.
entries.evidence: Juzek & Ward name it as focal word; Liang et al. top-four LLM word.
entries.example: The scheduler has an intricate interplay between queues.
entries.replacement_hint: Describe the interaction: 'The queue depth and thermal limit interact.'
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Sometimes the correct technical word for a layout.

entries.why: Vague importance adjective with high LLM preference.
entries.evidence: Liang et al. top-four LLM word; Wikipedia lists 'pivotal' in puffery.
entries.example: Quantization is a pivotal step in the pipeline.
entries.replacement_hint: State the effect: 'Quantization cut latency 2x.'

entries.why: Self-praise for care that readers discount; describes nothing about the method.
entries.evidence: Kobak Fig S6 excess set; antislop-sampler list has 'meticulous' and 'meticulously'.
entries.example: I ran each case with meticulous care.
entries.replacement_hint: Describe the procedure: 'I ran each case three times and kept the median.'

entries.why: Praise adjective that signals empty evaluation.
entries.evidence: Kobak Fig S6 rare excess set (membership only, no ratio).
entries.example: The team's commendable effort made the release possible.
entries.replacement_hint: Cut it, or name the work.

entries.why: Stock importance marker in the common excess-word set.
entries.evidence: Kobak v5 Fig 2b delta=0.037; Wikipedia crucial/pivotal/vital puffery.
entries.example: Thermal headroom is crucial for sustained throughput.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what happens without it, with the number.

entries.why: Sentence-opening emphasis that LLMs insert to signal importance.
entries.evidence: Kobak v5 Sec 2.2 common excess-word set includes 'notably'.
entries.example: Notably, the fp16 path had no regressions.
entries.replacement_hint: State the surprising fact directly.

entries.why: Padding connector at sentence start, frequent in LLM output.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia 2023-mid 2024 list ('Additionally'); Originality.ai raw count (no rate).
entries.example: Additionally, the run used 4 GB of memory.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the fact, or write 'Also'.

entries.why: Claims completeness without listing what was covered.
entries.evidence: Kobak v5 Sec 2.2 common excess set; listed in Stockton and Brafton stock-vocabulary lists.
entries.example: This is a comprehensive benchmark suite.
entries.replacement_hint: List the models, devices and cases covered.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Legitimate for a test suite that is actually broad.

entries.why: Emphasis filler LLMs insert in a steady rhythm.
entries.evidence: Kobak v5 Sec 2.2 common excess-word set.
entries.example: The cache is particularly sensitive to stride changes.
entries.replacement_hint: Delete, or give the number.

entries.why: Vague improvement verb with no stated magnitude.
entries.evidence: Kobak v5 excess set; Wikipedia AI vocabulary and promotional list.
entries.example: Fusing the norm layer enhances throughput on the ANE.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the measured change: 'raised throughput from 210 to 290 tokens/s'.

entries.why: Formal substitute for 'showed', typical of LLM academic register.
entries.evidence: Kobak v5 Sec 2.2 common excess set.
entries.example: The model exhibited a 12% drop in accuracy.
entries.replacement_hint: 'showed' or 'had'.

entries.why: Abstract noun for findings common in LLM summary voice.
entries.evidence: Kobak v5 Sec 2.2 common excess set.
entries.example: These insights point to a scheduler bottleneck.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the result.

entries.why: Formal verb named as an LLM-associated word.
entries.evidence: Holzwarth et al. (2026 preprint) name it; no frequency given.
entries.example: Memory pressure is exacerbating the thermal throttle.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what increases: 'Memory pressure lowers the throttle point.'

entries.why: Superlative praise that LLMs favour.
entries.evidence: Holzwarth et al. name it as uncommon LLM vocabulary; no frequency given.
entries.example: The trace log was invaluable for finding the stall.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what it showed: 'The trace showed the stall at dispatch 14.'

entries.why: Em dashes are the most cited LLM punctuation tell, used where humans use commas or parentheses.
entries.evidence: Freeburg (arXiv 2603.27006): 0.0 to 9.1 per 1,000 words across models (LLM only, no human baseline). Wikipedia: used more than typical human prose.
entries.example: The result was fast—about 3 ms—but the variance was high.
entries.replacement_hint: Gate on density per 1,000 words, not presence. Use a comma, colon or parentheses.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Density signal only; a single em dash is normal writing.

entries.why: Spaced en dash used as an em-dash substitute.
entries.evidence: Local anti-slop rules flag this form; unspaced ranges are legitimate.
entries.example: The loader is fast – but the decoder is the limit.
entries.replacement_hint: Use a full stop, comma or colon.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Unspaced ranges are excluded by the pattern.

entries.pattern: (?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:in conclusion|to summarize|to put it simply|in essence)\b
entries.why: Sentence-initial summary label announcing a recap the text does not need.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler: 'in conclusion', 'in summary', 'to summarize' each 0.03125; Wikipedia words-to-watch list.
entries.example: In summary, the ANE path wins above batch size 8.
entries.replacement_hint: Put the result in the last sentence and drop the label.

entries.why: Formal connective LLM text reuses heavily.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler: 'moreover' and 'furthermore' each 0.03125.
entries.example: Moreover, the cache hit rate dropped after the update.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the next fact, or write 'Also'.

entries.pattern: \bit(?:'|’)?s (?:important|worth|essential|crucial) to (?:note|noting|remember|consider)\b|\bit(?:'|’)?s worth noting\b|\bit is worth noting\b|\bimportant to note\b
entries.why: Didactic signpost that flags a point without making it.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler: 'it's important to note', 'it's worth noting that' each 0.03125; Wikipedia 'important to note' disclaimers.
entries.example: It's worth noting that the warm-up run is excluded.
entries.replacement_hint: Put the fact in the sentence.

entries.why: Stock opener that delays the claim.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler list: 'when it comes to' 0.03125.
entries.example: When it comes to latency, the ANE wins.
entries.replacement_hint: 'For latency, the ANE wins.'

entries.why: Generic framing opener that fits any topic.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler: 'in today's digital age/era' each 0.03125; Brafton and Stop-slop list variants.
entries.example: In today's digital age, on-device inference matters.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the specific claim.

entries.why: Grand scope phrase that adds no information.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler: 'in the realm of' 0.03125.
entries.example: In the realm of on-device ML, latency is the constraint.
entries.replacement_hint: 'For on-device ML, latency is the constraint.'

entries.why: Generic scope phrase typical of LLM openers.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler: 'in the world of' 0.03125; YourTango lists it as filler.
entries.example: In the world of Core ML, conversion is the hard part.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the domain directly.

entries.why: Scene-setting metaphor for a field, used to sound broad.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'landscape'; Wikipedia 'evolving landscape' puffery; Carly and Stockton list 'digital landscape'.
entries.example: In today's evolving landscape of edge AI...
entries.replacement_hint: Name the specific tool or change.

entries.why: Vague field metaphor listed in AI vocabulary.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia AI vocabulary list (excerpt).
entries.example: The Core ML landscape changed with the new compiler.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the tool or vendor.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Literal uses such as a 'performance landscape' are fine.

entries.why: Swaps plain 'is' for fancier verbs, a documented LLM pattern.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia copulative avoidance: 'serves as', 'stands as', 'functions as' in place of 'is'.
entries.example: The cache serves as a buffer between stages.
entries.replacement_hint: 'is a buffer'.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: 'serves as' is sometimes correct; check each hit.

entries.why: Brochure verb for features.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia promotional and copula lists ('boasts a').
entries.example: The board boasts a 16-core Neural Engine.
entries.replacement_hint: 'has'.

entries.pattern: \b(?:is a|a|stands as a|serves as a) testament (?:to|of)\b|\bis a (?:testament|reminder) (?:to|of)\b
entries.why: Inflated significance formula that adds weight without a fact.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'testament to' 0.03125; Wikipedia 'is a testament/reminder'.
entries.example: The 2x gain is a testament to the new kernel.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what the number shows.

entries.why: Textbook AI metaphor for connected elements.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'tapestry'/'tapestries' 0.03125; Wikipedia AI vocabulary; The Conversation.
entries.example: The stack is a tapestry of kernels and copies.
entries.replacement_hint: List the parts.

entries.why: Inflates a plain start into a journey.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'embark' 0.03125.
entries.example: We embark on a benchmark of the new compiler.
entries.replacement_hint: 'start' or 'ran'.

entries.why: Stock adjective for integration claims the text never demonstrates.
entries.evidence: Stockton and claudemarketers lists; local copy and lint rules flag it.
entries.example: The handoff between the two models is seamless.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what crosses the boundary and what it costs.

entries.why: Overstated change claim with no measured change.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'transformative' 0.1017; Stockton and Microcopy lists.
entries.example: Batching was a transformative change for throughput.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the number: 'Batching raised throughput 3.1x.'

entries.why: Abstract verb LLM text uses for 'is the basis of'.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'underpins' 0.03125.
entries.example: The scheduler underpins the whole pipeline.
entries.replacement_hint: 'the pipeline depends on the scheduler'.

entries.why: Hype verb promising hidden power without naming a change.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'unleash' 0.03125; Stockton and Microcopy lists; local lint rules.
entries.example: The update unleashes the full Neural Engine.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what runs where.

entries.why: Stock promise verb of product copy.
entries.evidence: Local anti-slop rules list 'unlock the/your/a/new' as benefit-speak; Stockton flags 'unlock'.
entries.example: Unlock the full potential of your measurements.
entries.replacement_hint: Name what the reader can now see or do.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Functional 'unlock with Face ID' is spared by the pattern.

entries.why: Marketing intensifier without a number.
entries.evidence: Stockton, Microcopy, claudemarketers and local copy rules list it.
entries.example: Supercharge your Core ML pipeline.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the measured speedup and its condition.

entries.why: Speed metaphor with no measurement.
entries.evidence: Local lint and rules lists.
entries.example: This turbocharges decode on the M-series GPU.
entries.replacement_hint: Give before and after times with the workload named.

entries.why: Generic uplift verb of landing copy.
entries.evidence: Local copy and rules lists; narrowed to avoid technical 'elevate privilege' use.
entries.example: Our tooling elevates your workflow.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the improvement.

entries.why: Abstract uplift verb naming no capability.
entries.evidence: Stockton, Microcopy, claudemarketers and local copy lists.
entries.example: This API empowers teams to ship faster.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what the user can now do.

entries.why: Stock hype phrase.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'harness' entry.
entries.example: We harness the power of the Neural Engine.
entries.replacement_hint: 'run on the Neural Engine'.

entries.why: Modernity claim that names no version or number.
entries.evidence: Five opened sources list it (Stockton, Microcopy, PR News, claudemarketers, aisdr).
entries.example: A cutting-edge chip for on-device inference.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the chip, generation and measured number.

entries.why: Generic hype noun asserting importance.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'game changer' 0.03125; Stockton, Microcopy and Stop-slop lists.
entries.example: Quantization is a game changer for this model.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the measured effect.

entries.why: Stock adjective for communities and ecosystems in LLM text.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'vibrant' 0.03125; Wikipedia promotional list.
entries.example: The vibrant open-source ecosystem supports Core ML.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the project and its activity.

entries.why: Promotional intensifier in AI puffery lists.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia promotional list ('profound'); quoted list, no rate.
entries.example: The result has profound implications for on-device ML.
entries.replacement_hint: State the implication.

entries.why: Inflated 'shows' in promotional text.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia promotional list ('exemplifies').
entries.example: The fused kernel exemplifies the new scheduling model.
entries.replacement_hint: 'shows'.

entries.why: Intensifier for a problem that is not described.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'daunting' 0.03125.
entries.example: Converting the graph is a daunting task.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the blocker.

entries.why: Scene-setting adjective with no claim attached.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'ever-evolving', 'everchanging' 0.03125; Stockton and aisdr.
entries.example: In this ever-evolving field, benchmarks age quickly.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the change or delete.

entries.why: Describes intent instead of the result.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'designed to enhance' 0.03125.
entries.example: The patch is designed to enhance cache reuse.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what changed and what it measured.

entries.why: Stock signpost verb close to 'delve'.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 'dive into' 0.03125.
entries.example: Let's dive into the scheduler.
entries.replacement_hint: 'Here is the scheduler'.

entries.why: Stock back-reference a plain writer would not use.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 0.03125.
entries.example: As previously mentioned, the warm-up run is excluded.
entries.replacement_hint: Restate the fact in one clause.

entries.why: Announces considerations without listing them.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler 0.03125.
entries.example: There are a few considerations when converting to Core ML.
entries.replacement_hint: List them, or skip the announcement.

entries.pattern: \bas an? (?:ai )?(?:language model|assistant)\b|\bas an ai,|\bas a large language model\b
entries.why: Chatbot self-reference that a human author never writes.
entries.evidence: AlpinDale gptslop lists 'As an AI'; Originality.ai quotes 'As a large language model'; Wikipedia.
entries.example: As an AI language model, I can't run the benchmark.
entries.replacement_hint: Delete; state the actual limitation.

entries.why: Chatbot self-description.
entries.evidence: Originality.ai quotes a ChatGPT reply using the phrase.
entries.example: My training data includes few examples of this op.
entries.replacement_hint: Delete; name the actual dataset.

entries.why: Chatbot refusal opener.
entries.evidence: AlpinDale gptslop lists it.
entries.example: I'm sorry, but I couldn't reproduce the timing.
entries.replacement_hint: State the result.

entries.why: Assistant acknowledgement opener.
entries.evidence: Originality.ai: every reply to three test questions opened with 'Absolutely!' (n=3); Wikipedia lists 'Certainly!', 'Of course!'.
entries.example: Certainly! Here is the revised benchmark table.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the content.

entries.pattern: \bi hope this (?:helps|message finds you well)\b|\bi (?:hope|trust) this message finds you well\b
entries.why: Assistant sign-off that does not belong in a research post.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia lists the phrases verbatim.
entries.example: I hope this helps clarify the numbers.
entries.replacement_hint: Delete.

entries.pattern: \bwould you like (?:me to|to)\b|\bis there anything else\b|\blet me know if (?:you|there)\b
entries.why: Offer-to-help closer typical of chat assistants.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia lists 'Would you like...', 'is there anything else', 'let me know'.
entries.example: Let me know if you want the raw traces.
entries.replacement_hint: Link the raw data instead.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Human email uses it, not research prose.

entries.pattern: \bi (?:can(?:'|’)?t|cannot) (?:offer|provide) (?:medical|legal|financial) advice\b|\b(?:up to|as of) my last (?:training|knowledge) update\b
entries.why: Refusal and cutoff boilerplate from chat assistants.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia lists both verbatim.
entries.example: As of my last knowledge update, the API was in beta.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the date you checked the source.

entries.pattern: \b(?:experts argue|some experts believe|some critics argue|industry reports (?:show|suggest|indicate)|observers have (?:cited|noted)|it could be argued that|one might say)\b
entries.why: Unnamed authority borrowed to add weight.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia vague-attribution list (verbatim); HowManyWords hedging list.
entries.example: Experts argue that on-device inference will dominate.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the source or drop the claim.

entries.why: Challenges template that ends in vague positivity.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia challenge formula: 'Despite its... faces several challenges'.
entries.example: Despite these challenges, the port is promising.
entries.replacement_hint: List the two or three concrete limits.

entries.why: Section-title template typical of generated outlines.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia lists 'Challenges and Legacy' and 'Future Outlook' as headers.
entries.example: ## Future Outlook
entries.replacement_hint: Name the next concrete experiment.

entries.why: Markdown Conclusion section is a legacy LLM template.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia: older LLMs added sections titled 'Conclusion'.
entries.example: ## Conclusion
entries.replacement_hint: End on the result or the open question.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: A real research report may keep one.

entries.why: Tacked-on -ing clause that adds interpretation without evidence.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia superficial analyses list; Stockton takeaways.
entries.example: The benchmark ran on 8 cores, highlighting the scaling limits.
entries.replacement_hint: End at the measured limit, or make it its own sentence.

entries.why: Symbolism formula with no content.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia verbatim list.
entries.example: The project opened a repo, symbolizing its ongoing commitment.
entries.replacement_hint: Delete the clause.

entries.why: Empty praise for the reader's takeaway.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia superficial-analysis list (verbatim).
entries.example: The run yields valuable insights into thermal limits.
entries.replacement_hint: State the specific finding.

entries.why: Vague fit claim in place of a comparison.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia superficial-analysis list.
entries.example: The latency curve aligns with the theoretical model.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the measured gap from the model.

entries.pattern: \b(?:setting the stage for|indelible mark|deeply rooted|evolving landscape|key turning point|watershed moment|pivotal moment|lasting (?:legacy|impact))\b
entries.why: Broad-significance language that inflates importance.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia puffery list; Stockton takeaways.
entries.example: This release marks a watershed moment for on-device AI.
entries.replacement_hint: State the change in plain words.

entries.why: Canned role statement with no mechanism.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia significance list (verbatim); Stockton takeaways.
entries.example: The scheduler plays a vital role in throughput.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what it does and the effect.

entries.why: Overstated framing of a change.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia significance list.
entries.example: The release marks a key turning point for on-device inference.
entries.replacement_hint: Describe what changed on the device.

entries.why: Ties a narrow finding to a vague trend.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia significance list (verbatim).
entries.example: The regression reflects broader trends in model design.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the trend with a source, or cut.

entries.why: Abstract noun that replaces naming the specific problem.
entries.evidence: antislop-sampler: 'complexities' 0.03125, 'intricacies' 0.1032, 'nuances' 0.1120.
entries.example: Given the complexities of ANE scheduling, we measured each layer.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the scheduler, cache or dtype issue.

entries.why: Claims difficulty without naming it.
entries.evidence: YourTango, HowManyWords and Stop-slop lists.
entries.example: While navigating the complexities of memory layout, we found a bug.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the specific difficulty.

entries.why: Source-availability hedge in place of a stated limitation.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia verbatim list.
entries.example: Based on available information, the driver is not publicly documented.
entries.replacement_hint: Say which source you checked and what it does not show.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Real documentation gaps are often true; check each.

entries.why: Announces missing information instead of stating it.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia words-to-watch list (verbatim).
entries.example: While specific details are limited, the chip is believed to use 16 cores.
entries.replacement_hint: State what is known, with its source, and mark the gap once.

entries.pattern: \bmaintains a low profile\b|\bkeeps personal details private\b
entries.why: Biographical filler from LLM output.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia verbatim list.
entries.example: The engineer maintains a low profile.
entries.replacement_hint: Cut, or state a citable fact.

entries.why: Announces a fixed list count that LLMs fill in.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia mid-2026 section (verbatim).
entries.example: There are three main factors behind the slowdown:
entries.replacement_hint: Write the factors that matter, in prose.

entries.why: Parallel construction listed under LLM language patterns.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia negative parallelisms list.
entries.example: The tool not only compiles the model but also profiles it.
entries.replacement_hint: Two plain sentences.

entries.why: Contrast against a supposed misconception, overused by LLMs.
entries.evidence: EQ-Bench Slop Score weights not-X-but-Y at 25%; Wikipedia 3.3.
entries.example: This is not just a faster kernel, but a different scheduler.
entries.replacement_hint: State the one claim.

entries.why: Named LLM construction that denies a claim nobody made, then supplies a replacement.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia 3.3 negative parallelisms; Stockton calls it the most prominent tell; EQ-Bench.
entries.example: It's not a faster chip. It's a different memory model.
entries.replacement_hint: State the positive claim alone.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Legitimate contrast in corrections exists; review.

entries.why: Parallel negation stack named as an LLM pattern.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia verbatim pattern.
entries.example: No setup, no tuning, just run it.
entries.replacement_hint: One plain sentence.

entries.why: Repeated subject negation drumbeat that stands in for a claim.
entries.evidence: Owner rejected this chain on 2026-11-08 (owner statement, not a fetched source).
entries.example: Speed is not the point. Speed is not the goal. Speed is not the metric.
entries.replacement_hint: Keep one negation only if it corrects a real misreading.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Backreference is case-insensitive under the i flag.

entries.why: Stock correction opener that asserts a bigger identity.
entries.evidence: Local copy guide lists 'More than a ...' as a shape to avoid.
entries.example: More than a tool, it is a workflow.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what the tool does in one sentence.

entries.why: Emoji as icon or bullet is a generated-text sign and renders differently per platform.
entries.evidence: Local lint and rules flag emoji as UI; Wikipedia lists emoji on headings and list items.
entries.example: 🚀 Faster compile times
entries.replacement_hint: Use words. Strip emoji from prose and list markers.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Requires the u flag. Emoji_Presentation excludes the copyright sign.

entries.why: Dramatic noun-phrase heading that teases a section instead of naming it.
entries.evidence: realross README bans 'The Pricing Trap' and 'The Hidden Cost of Convenience'.
entries.example: ## The Hidden Cost of Speed
entries.replacement_hint: Name the section: '## Energy cost per inference'.

entries.why: Bulleted list with bold lead-in labels is a named generated-text habit.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia bolded bullet lists; Stockton excessive boldface.
entries.example: - **Latency:** 12 ms
entries.replacement_hint: Plain bullets, or put the number first.

entries.why: Markdown bold residue in running prose.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia: asterisks used for bold in prose flagged as a sign.
entries.example: The **key result** is a 2x speedup.
entries.replacement_hint: Remove the asterisks.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Fine in a markdown renderer that uses it for emphasis; check the site.

entries.why: Markdown section dividers in prose are an AI-output artifact.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia markup list (verbatim).
entries.replacement_hint: Use a real heading or nothing.

entries.why: Unfilled template placeholder.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia lists '2026-xx-xx' and INSERT_SOURCE_URL placeholders verbatim.
entries.example: Measured on 2026-xx-xx.
entries.replacement_hint: Fill in the real date or URL.

entries.why: Assistant-origin tracking tag pasted with a link.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia lists the tags verbatim.
entries.example: See https://example.com/post?utm_source=chatgpt.com
entries.replacement_hint: Strip the tag.

entries.why: Promotional brochure vocabulary that Wikipedia ties to AI text.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia promotional list (verbatim); Stockton takeaways; PR News list for groundbreaking.
entries.example: The lab is nestled in the hills.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the location plainly.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Low. 'groundbreaking' can describe a real result, so check it.

entries.why: Brochure phrase with no content.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia promotional list (verbatim).
entries.example: The lab shows a commitment to excellence.
entries.replacement_hint: Cut it.

entries.pattern: \bindependent coverage\b|\bwritten by a leading expert\b|\bactive social media presence\b
entries.why: Notability boilerplate that asserts credibility without a source.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia verbatim list.
entries.example: The author is a leading expert with an active social media presence.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the credential and link it, or cut.

entries.why: Product label that carries no technical content.
entries.evidence: Microcopy Examples and local copy guide quote the mad-lib shape.
entries.example: An AI-powered platform for research teams.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the model, the task and what it runs on.

entries.why: Superlative category labels common in product and press copy.
entries.evidence: Stockton, PR News, local lint and copy lists.
entries.example: A best-in-class, next-generation accelerator.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the spec and the measured efficiency.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: 'next-generation' can name a real chip generation; check it.

entries.why: Overstated change language used in press releases and AI copy.
entries.evidence: Stockton, Microcopy, PR News and aisdr lists.
entries.example: A revolutionary approach to on-device ML.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what changed and by how much.

entries.why: Self-praise adjective with no content of its own.
entries.evidence: Stockton, Microcopy and PR News lists.
entries.example: Our innovative method beats the baseline.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the method and the baseline number.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Some papers use it; this site should not.

entries.why: Vague praise adjective on AI vocabulary lists.
entries.evidence: Stockton and Brafton stock-vocabulary lists.
entries.example: The ANE is a powerful accelerator for this model.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the throughput or energy number.

entries.why: Generic importance adjective that often stands in for a reason.
entries.evidence: Stockton, Brafton and YourTango lists.
entries.example: Warm-up is essential for stable timing.
entries.replacement_hint: State the consequence: 'Without warm-up the first run is 2x slower.'

entries.why: Abstract growth verb LLMs use for generic benefits.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia AI vocabulary; Stockton; claudemarketers.
entries.example: The design fosters collaboration between teams.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what the design makes possible.

entries.why: Formal 'attract' verb listed in 2023-24 AI vocabulary.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia 2023 to mid-2024 list (verbatim).
entries.example: The post garnered wide attention.
entries.replacement_hint: 'got', or state the count.

entries.why: Adjective used to imply lasting significance.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia 2023 to mid-2024 list (verbatim).
entries.example: The method has enduring value for researchers.
entries.replacement_hint: Cut it, or state the time span.

entries.why: Abstract noun that hand-waves at relationships.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia AI vocabulary list (excerpt).
entries.example: The interplay between cache and bandwidth matters.
entries.replacement_hint: Say how one changes the other, with a number.

entries.why: Inflates apparent complexity and leads into padded explanation.
entries.evidence: aisdr names it; claudemarketers preview; Wikipedia later-era list.
entries.example: Power management is a multifaceted problem.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the facets, or say 'complex' if it is.

entries.why: Corporate verb on AI vocabulary and press-release cliche lists.
entries.evidence: PR News list; Stockton; Wikipedia later-era list; local lint list.
entries.example: We leverage the NPU for the attention block.
entries.replacement_hint: Write 'use', and name the mechanism.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: The physics or literal technical sense is legitimate.

entries.why: Generic quality adjective that stands in for the test that showed it.
entries.evidence: Wikipedia, Stockton, claudemarketers and local copy lists.
entries.example: The harness gives robust results across seeds.
entries.replacement_hint: State the variance or the seed count.

entries.why: Abstraction that signals a summary rather than a claim.
entries.evidence: Local lint list.
entries.example: We take a holistic view of latency.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the components measured together.

entries.why: Stock abstraction that names no mechanism.
entries.evidence: Local lint list.
entries.example: The two kernels show synergy.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the mechanism and the measured combined effect.

entries.why: Efficiency verb that claims improvement without a metric.
entries.evidence: Stockton, claudemarketers and local copy and lint lists.
entries.example: This script streamlines the benchmark workflow.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the removed step and the time saved.

entries.why: Reframing verb that promises novelty without naming a change.
entries.evidence: Local lint list; copy guide 'X, reimagined' headline shape.
entries.example: We reimagine the attention kernel.
entries.replacement_hint: Say what the kernel does now that it did not before.

entries.why: Ease claim that replaces the actual steps.
entries.evidence: Local copy, lint and rules lists.
entries.example: Converting a model is effortless.
entries.replacement_hint: Count the steps or commands the conversion takes.

entries.why: Speed adjective that replaces a measured time.
entries.evidence: Local lint and copy lists.
entries.example: The loader is blazing fast.
entries.replacement_hint: Write the load time in ms on a named device.

entries.why: Superiority claim with no comparison attached.
entries.evidence: PR News list of overused press-release phrases.
entries.example: Our model reaches state-of-the-art accuracy on the test set.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the number and the baseline.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Legitimate when a benchmark and baseline follow.

entries.why: Big-change phrase rarely supported in its own sentence.
entries.evidence: Ruben Hassid list; claudemarketers.
entries.example: This is a paradigm shift for edge inference.
entries.replacement_hint: State the change in one concrete sentence.

entries.why: Upgrade phrase from landing copy.
entries.evidence: Local lint and rules lists.
entries.example: Take your benchmarks to the next level.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the new capability and its measured limit.

entries.why: Staged before-and-after with no content.
entries.evidence: Local lint list.
entries.example: Say goodbye to slow exports.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the measured export time.

entries.why: Catalogue audience phrase.
entries.evidence: Local lint list.
entries.example: A notebook built for the modern researcher.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the person and the task.

entries.why: Stock audience phrase that fits any product.
entries.evidence: Local copy guide mad-lib example.
entries.example: Built for modern teams.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the team or role.

entries.why: Greeting used as a headline in place of a claim.
entries.evidence: Local copy guide lists 'Welcome to ...'.
entries.example: Welcome to the ANE lab.
entries.replacement_hint: Open with what the lab measured.

entries.why: Mad-lib headline with no content.
entries.evidence: Local copy guide: 'X, reimagined / redefined / made simple'.
entries.example: Inference, reimagined.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the thing and its one specific difference.

entries.why: Announcement emotion from press or social copy.
entries.evidence: Stockton and PR News lists.
entries.example: We are thrilled to share our latest benchmark.
entries.replacement_hint: Lead with the result.

entries.why: Audience-address formula that reads as ad copy.
entries.evidence: YourTango lists both forms.
entries.example: Whether you're a researcher or a student, look no further.
entries.replacement_hint: Address the reader's task directly.

entries.why: Padding that adds word count without meaning.
entries.evidence: YourTango filler list.
entries.example: There is a plethora of Core ML tools.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the count or name the tools.

entries.why: Sales-style question closer.
entries.evidence: Microcopy Examples lists 'Ready to...?'.
entries.example: Ready to speed up your models?
entries.replacement_hint: Delete, or state the benefit as a fact.

entries.why: Chatty intensifier from generated product copy.
entries.evidence: Microcopy Examples template.
entries.example: Oh-so-fast inference.
entries.replacement_hint: Give the latency.

entries.why: Background sentence that delays the point.
entries.evidence: Brafton lists it as formulaic introduction.
entries.example: As technology continues to evolve, edge AI matters more.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the measurement.

entries.why: Passive hedge that avoids naming who showed something.
entries.evidence: Brafton lists 'It is often said that' as passive filler.
entries.example: It is often said that ANE kernels are faster.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the source or state the measurement.

entries.why: Scene-setting phrase that delays the claim.
entries.evidence: Stop-slop phrase list.
entries.example: At its core, the problem is memory bandwidth.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the bottleneck directly.

entries.why: Scene-setting opener that delays the claim.
entries.evidence: Stop-slop and Ruben Hassid lists.
entries.example: In a world where chips are fast, memory matters.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the bottleneck.

entries.why: Build-up line that performs a reveal.
entries.evidence: Stop-slop, claudemarketers and Ruben Hassid lists.
entries.example: Here's the thing: the ANE is faster only above batch 4.
entries.replacement_hint: Put the claim first.

entries.why: Poses and answers its own question.
entries.evidence: Stockton list ('the goal?', 'the result?').
entries.example: The result? The ANE finished the batch in 4 ms.
entries.replacement_hint: Write the result without the question.

entries.pattern: \b(?:let me be clear|the uncomfortable truth is|i['’]ll say it again|i['’]m going to be honest)\b
entries.why: Credibility signpost that adds no information.
entries.evidence: Stop-slop phrase list.
entries.example: The uncomfortable truth is that the benchmark was wrong.
entries.replacement_hint: State the correction directly.

entries.pattern: \b(?:let that sink in|make no mistake|this matters because)\b|\bfull stop\.
entries.why: Emphasis performed in words instead of earned.
entries.evidence: Stop-slop emphasis list.
entries.example: Make no mistake: the cache is the bottleneck.
entries.replacement_hint: Show the measurement that makes the point.

entries.why: Reveal label that mimics a narrative hook.
entries.evidence: Stop-slop meta-commentary list.
entries.example: Spoiler: the ANE wins on energy.
entries.replacement_hint: State the result without a label.

entries.pattern: \blet me walk you through\b|\bin this (?:article|section|post),? we['’]ll\b
entries.why: Signposts the document instead of writing its content.
entries.evidence: Stop-slop and Wikipedia editorializing lists.
entries.example: In this article, we'll walk through the conversion.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the conversion step.

entries.pattern: \b(?:lean into|circle back|on the same page|moving forward|take a step back)\b
entries.why: Corporate idiom that reads as workplace filler.
entries.evidence: Stop-slop business jargon list.
entries.example: Let's double down on the scheduler.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the action.

entries.why: Narrative hook from novels and ad copy.
entries.evidence: Carly lists 'Picture this:' as a giveaway.
entries.example: Picture this: a model that runs on a phone.
entries.replacement_hint: Start with the model and device.

entries.why: Staged-intimacy or social-proof labels that assert without naming anyone.
entries.evidence: Local copy and tells guides list these labels.
entries.example: Quietly trusted by researchers.
entries.replacement_hint: Delete, or name a real user with permission.

entries.why: Editorial label applied to ordinary content to borrow authority.
entries.evidence: Local copy and tells guides.
entries.example: Field notes: ANE dispatch overhead.
entries.replacement_hint: Use 'Notes' or the subject itself.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Legitimate if the site really keeps a field-notes series.

entries.why: Decorative chrome that adds no content.
entries.evidence: Local copy and tells guides list these as furniture text.
entries.example: (Scroll to explore)
entries.replacement_hint: Delete it.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Requires the m flag for the line-anchored forms.

entries.why: Words joined by middle dots read as generated chrome.
entries.evidence: Local copy and tells guides.
entries.example: Research · Benchmarks · Field notes
entries.replacement_hint: Write a sentence, or a plain list.

entries.why: Liveness badge that the page does not have.
entries.evidence: Local anti-slop rules.
entries.example: LIVE · 09:41 Benchmark running
entries.replacement_hint: Remove, or state the real run start time with date.

entries.why: Padded stage labels duplicate the order of the content.
entries.evidence: Local copy guide and lint rule.
entries.example: Phase 02: decode
entries.replacement_hint: Use the stage's own name or an ordered list.

entries.why: Paired index numbers are decorative scaffolding when order carries no meaning.
entries.evidence: Local tells and rules guides.
entries.example: 01 / Dispatch 02 / Memory
entries.replacement_hint: Drop the numbers.

entries.why: A 99.9% figure without denominator or source is decorative precision.
entries.evidence: Local anti-slop rules list invented-evidence shapes.
entries.example: Our pipeline is 99.9% accurate.
entries.replacement_hint: State the measurement, denominator and test set.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Real measured figures are legitimate; check.

entries.why: Unsourced magnitude claim.
entries.evidence: Local anti-slop rules list 10x and 100x as invented-evidence shapes.
entries.example: It runs 10x faster.
entries.replacement_hint: Write the two measured times, workload and device.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Matches real measured ratios; needs a cited baseline check.

entries.why: Ranking claim with no ranking source.
entries.evidence: Local anti-slop rules list it.
entries.example: The #1 choice for on-device research.
entries.replacement_hint: Delete, or cite the ranking.

entries.why: Round user counts with no named users are invented social proof.
entries.evidence: Local rules, tells and copy guides.
entries.example: Trusted by thousands of researchers.
entries.replacement_hint: Delete it. Use only proof that is true and named.

entries.why: Caption that narrates the design look instead of the content.
entries.evidence: Local copy guide lists it.
entries.example: A clean, minimal layout for comparing benchmarks.
entries.replacement_hint: Describe the axes, workload and result.

entries.pattern: follow the evidence|look beneath the claim|evidence before inference|research, not a victory lap|build\. experiment\. understand|make the question inspectable
entries.why: Slogans the owner rejected for generic exhortation with no work named.
entries.evidence: Owner rejected these on 2026-11-08 (owner statement, not a fetched source).
entries.example: Our work tests the decode path. Follow the evidence.
entries.replacement_hint: State the specific result or the measurement that supports the claim.

entries.why: Template error copy that names no failure.
entries.evidence: Local anti-slop rules.
entries.example: Oops! Something went wrong.
entries.replacement_hint: State the failure and the next step.

entries.why: Abandoned filler that makes a page look unfinished.
entries.evidence: Local lint, rules and tells guides.
entries.example: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.
entries.replacement_hint: Write one real sentence.

entries.why: Trailing arrow on a short label is the reflex call-to-action glyph.
entries.evidence: Local copy guide: at most one arrow, on the primary action.
entries.example: See the per-layer timings →
entries.replacement_hint: Drop the arrow.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Flow diagrams use arrows; requires the m flag.

entries.why: Link or button label that names no destination.
entries.evidence: Local lint and tells lists.
entries.example: Latency results. Learn more.
entries.replacement_hint: Name the destination, e.g. 'See the per-layer timings'.
entries.technical_false_positive_risk: Some sites use these labels legitimately.

entries.why: Link label with no information about the destination.
entries.evidence: Local lint list.
entries.example: For the raw logs, click here.
entries.replacement_hint: Put the destination in the link text.
